sentences.zh: 初紅苗犯鎮筸，游擊沈長祿往剿，至大梅山，守備許邦垣、千總孫清俱陷賊，長祿私贖之歸，諱不報；

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Red Miao invaded Zhenqian, Mobile Corps Commander Shen Changlu went to suppress them; at Damei Mountain, Garrison Commander Xu Bangyuan and Battalion Commander Sun Qing both fell into enemy hands; Changlu privately ransomed them back and concealed it without reporting;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Red Miao invaded Zhenqian, Mobile Corps Commander Shen Changlu went to suppress them. At Damei Mountain, Garrison Commander Xu Bangyuan and Battalion Commander Sun Qing both fell into enemy hands. Changlu privately ransomed them back and concealed it without reporting;

sentences.zh: 而副將硃紱報苗已就撫，琇據以入告。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Deputy Commander Zhu Fu reported the Miao had submitted to pacification, and Guo Xiu reported this to the throne on that basis.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Deputy Commander Zhu Fu reported the Miao had submitted to pacification, and Guo Xiu reported this to the throne on that basis.

sentences.zh: 繼祖等勘得狀，琇與提督林本植並奪官。

translations.literal: Jizu and the others verified the facts; Guo Xiu and Military Commissioner Lin Benzhi were both stripped of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Jizu and the others verified the facts. Guo Xiu and Military Commissioner Lin Benzhi were both stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year he died.

sentences.zh: 尋祀鄉賢，並祀吳江名宦。

translations.literal: Soon he was enshrined among local worthies and also among distinguished officials of Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was enshrined among local worthies and also among distinguished officials of Wujiang.

sentences.zh: 論曰：郝浴、楊素蘊秉剛正之性，抗論強籓，曲突徙薪，防禍未形，甘竄逐而不悔。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Hao Yu and Yang Suyun possessed upright and incorruptible natures; they argued against powerful frontier lords, bending the chimney and removing the fuel to prevent disaster before it took shape, and willingly accepted exile without regret.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Hao Yu and Yang Suyun possessed upright and incorruptible natures. They argued against powerful frontier lords, bending the chimney and removing the fuel to prevent disaster before it took shape, and willingly accepted exile without regret.

sentences.zh: 郭琇抨擊權相，有直臣之風，震霆一鳴，僉壬解體。

translations.literal: Guo Xiu attacked the powerful minister with the bearing of an upright official; one clap of thunder and the whole faction fell apart.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiu attacked the powerful minister with the bearing of an upright official. One clap of thunder and the whole faction fell apart.

sentences.zh: 蓋由聖祖已悟其奸，而琇遂得行其志。

translations.literal: This was because the Sage Ancestor had already perceived the minister's treachery, and so Guo Xiu was able to carry out his intent.
translations.idiomatic: This was because the Sage Ancestor had already perceived the minister's treachery, and so Guo Xiu was able to carry out his intent.

sentences.zh: 然以浴之廉，蒙議於身後；

translations.literal: Yet despite Hao Yu's integrity he was subjected to censure after death;
translations.idiomatic: Yet despite Hao Yu's integrity he was subjected to censure after death;

sentences.zh: 素蘊居官愛民，不終於位；

translations.literal: Yang Suyun loved the people in office but did not finish his term;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Suyun loved the people in office but did not finish his term;

sentences.zh: 琇則​​橫被誣陷，廢置十年，始獲申雪。

translations.literal: Guo Xiu was wantonly slandered and falsely accused, set aside for ten years before his name was finally cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiu was wantonly slandered and falsely accused, set aside for ten years before his name was finally cleared.

sentences.zh: 得君如聖祖，猶不克善全，直道難行，不其然哉？

translations.literal: Even with a sovereign like the Sage Ancestor they still could not be fully preserved in integrity — is it not so that the upright path is hard to walk?
translations.idiomatic: Even with a sovereign like the Sage Ancestor they still could not be fully preserved in integrity—is it not so that the upright path is hard to walk?
